claims.claim: Top-line readiness parity can hide controller dependence in local MLX Gemma tool-use runs.
claims.primary_metric: H1h/H1i no-directive readiness parity with high repair/fallback burden and low raw-clean rate.
claims.limitation: Current support is internal to Moonie's knowledge-work harness and local MLX runtime.
claims.next_test: Run the same helper-ablation structure on a harder H1 slice selected from raw replay failures.

claims.claim: The final tool-turn directive is causal for exact raw tool protocol behavior on the focused replay suite.
claims.primary_metric: Contracted exact replay is 7/8 while no-directive exact replay is 0/8 on the same cases.
claims.limitation: The replay suite is intentionally focused on eight observed no-directive failures, not a population estimate.
claims.next_test: Expand the replay suite with independently authored hard cases and repeated seeds.

claims.claim: Packaged workflow completion can wash out raw one-turn tool-protocol failures.
claims.primary_metric: H1j/H1k packaged packets saturated while exact replay still showed no-directive failures.
claims.limitation: The packaged workflow scaffolds may make the task easier than the one-turn replay contract.
claims.next_test: Build a harder packaged workflow slice that preserves one-turn parallel and visual follow-on pressure.

claims.claim: Tool-catalog role presentation changes visual routing behavior even without the exact tool-turn directive.
claims.primary_metric: visual_role_catalog_v1 moves latest-filter from wrong/no-call behavior to refine_selection argument mismatch.
claims.limitation: The intervention improves routing more than exact literal fidelity.
claims.next_test: Test catalog-role profiles across a larger visual follow-on set with fresh UI states.

claims.claim: Schema-local visual argument hints improve exact selector fidelity but can hurt executable visual-form recovery.
claims.primary_metric: v2 reaches 2/3 focused visual live exactness but loses executable form-target recovery.
claims.limitation: The improvement is focused on three visual replay cases and has a known form-target regression.
claims.next_test: Search for a split selector intervention that preserves v2 filter exactness and v1 form-target executability.

claims.claim: Adding broader split-selector wording did not recover the missing visual-form behavior and introduced a protocol-shape regression.
claims.primary_metric: v3 raw exact falls to 1/8 versus v2 at 2/8 and readback regresses through tool_name/name mismatch.
claims.limitation: This is one candidate profile; it does not rule out all field-specific selector interventions.
claims.next_test: Try an executor-grounded schema annotation or few-shot-free field contract that does not add broad behavioral prose.

claims.claim: Schema-local visual field hints are cleaner than broad selector prose but still do not recover executable form targeting.
claims.primary_metric: v4 ties v2 at 2/8 raw exact and preserves readback, but stays 0/1 executable and over-prefers refine_selection on form-target.
claims.limitation: This tests one schema-field annotation profile on the focused eight-case replay-derived probe.
claims.next_test: Create a fresh visual hard slice or constrain refine_selection preference only when a real selection_id is present.

claims.claim: A fresh visual hard slice breaks the earlier saturation and shows schema-field catalog hints can recover executable visual behavior without the exact directive.
claims.primary_metric: Contracted MLX reaches 8/8 strict, executable, and executor-equivalent; no-directive falls to 1/8; schema-field hints reach 6/8 strict and 8/8 executor-equivalent.
claims.limitation: The packet is eight independently authored visual cases, so it is stronger than design-only evidence but still not a population estimate.
claims.next_test: Promote v4 only after building a packaged H1 visual workflow that tests executor-visible success directly.

claims.claim: A narrow schema-target-literal repair did not improve hard-slice exactness and introduced a routing regression.
claims.primary_metric: v5 reaches 5/8 strict and 7/8 executor-equivalent versus v4 at 6/8 strict and 8/8 executor-equivalent; v5 adds one wrong-tool failure on the stale-selection decoy.
claims.limitation: This is still one eight-case hard-slice packet; it rejects the current wording, not all possible target-query exactness interventions.
claims.next_test: Do not iterate target-literal wording again until the stale-selection routing failure is isolated separately.

claims.claim: The remaining v4 visual hard-slice exact misses are executor-success selector aliases, not current evidence of failed visual targeting.
claims.primary_metric: v4 has 2/8 non-exact rows, both executor-target matches; first-class executor-equivalence scores v4 at 8/8 while benchmark-label artifact candidate count is 2 and true harness failure count is 0.
claims.limitation: This does not prove every visual selector paraphrase is acceptable; it only classifies the current hard-slice v4 misses under the local deterministic executor.
claims.next_test: Use the executor-equivalence score to design a packaged H1 visual workflow that separates executor success from strict protocol fidelity.

claims.claim: Promoting the visual executor-equivalence result into current packaged visual workflows does not yet preserve the hard-slice discrimination.
claims.primary_metric: H1l candidate rows tie at readiness 0.90406, strict interface 0.85, recovered execution 0.8, raw clean 1.0, and zero controller repair/fallback/argument repair.
claims.limitation: H1l uses existing staged packaged workflows, so it can reject this packaged surface without rejecting the hard-slice executor-equivalence signal.
claims.next_test: Preserve the hard-slice or exact-replay shape more faithfully in live operator execution before spending H1l helper-ablation budget.

claims.claim: Replay-shaped CLI-live execution preserves the visual hard-slice executor-equivalence signal that packaged H1l workflows washed out.
claims.primary_metric: On the two preserved no-directive visual hard-slice failures, no-directive is 0/2 strict and 0/2 executor-equivalent; contracted MLX is 2/2 strict and executor-equivalent; schema-field hints is the strongest no-directive row at 1/2 strict and 2/2 executor-equivalent.
claims.limitation: The live replay matrix covers the two preserved no-directive hard-slice failures, not the full eight-case hard-slice candidate matrix.
claims.next_test: Build a second replay-shaped live slice that repeats the executor-alias and stale-selection cases under harder decoys before returning to packaged H1 workflows.

claims.claim: A harder visual live stress replay preserves the executor-grounding advantage of schema-local catalog hints without improving strict protocol fidelity.
claims.primary_metric: On four fresh stress cases, no-directive MLX is 2/4 strict and 3/4 executor-equivalent; contracted MLX is 4/4 strict and executor-equivalent; schema-field hints and schema target literals are 2/4 strict but 4/4 executor-equivalent. On the 8-case alias-repeat follow-up, schema-field hints matches no-directive at 2/8 strict but improves executor-equivalence from 5/8 to 7/8, while schema target literals reach 3/8 strict and 8/8 executor-equivalent.
claims.limitation: The alias-repeat matrix is still one deterministic replay-shaped live packet, not a repeated stochastic estimate or a broad packaged workflow.
claims.next_test: Repeat the alias-repeat packet across seeds or promote only the surviving metric-panel/callout mechanisms into a non-saturated H1m packaged workflow.
